title: NIKATRU privacy declaration
description: The privacy declaration for one shipped surface — apps/<id>/privacy.yaml for an app, extensions/<Category>/<Tool>/publish/privacy.yaml for an extension. What it collects, why, for how long, and who else touches it, written ONCE in the discipline the sworn store declarations already use: every row carries the basis it was decided on, the source that basis was read from, and the date it was read. tooling/app-yaml/render-privacy.mjs renders the notice surfaces from it (the per-app privacy page and the Chrome Web Store privacy-practices disclosure); tooling/ci/assert-app-yaml.mjs grades it, holds the renderings byte-identical, and cross-checks the app rows against the two sworn declarations. The four sworn store JSON files are NOT rendered from it and never will be — [ADR 037]: a sworn declaration regenerated by a template is a statement nobody made.

app.description: The app id, or the extension slug. For an app it must equal app.yaml's `id`; for an extension it must equal publish/identity.json's `slug` — two files describing two different products is the one mistake a per-surface declaration makes easy.

surface.description: Which kind of shipped thing this declares. The two surfaces answer to different regulators with different vocabularies — an app answers Play's Data safety form and Apple's App Privacy questions, an extension answers the Chrome Web Store's Privacy practices tab — and the arity rules below differ because of that, not because one is graded more loosely. C-LOGIN-MANDATORY-IN-APPS is the same split, recorded for the same reason: the two surfaces genuinely differ.

state.description: APP SURFACE ONLY, and required there. Whether this app has made its privacy declaration yet. `pending` is what the app brick stamps: nobody has read this app's code, so it collects nothing it can name (`collects: []`), `asOf` is null, and render-privacy renders a short page saying the notice is not yet published. `declared` is a declaration somebody re-read against the code, with every rule below applying. A closed set, and a key rather than an inference: a missing `state` is a finding, never read as either value. O-BRICK-STAMPS-NO-PRIVACY-DECLARATION.

asOf.description: The date this declaration was last re-read against the code. Same {value, asOf, verify} discipline platform-state/ is built on. Null only on a `pending` app declaration, which has not been read against any code yet (see `allOf` below).

networkAddress.description: The published no-IP promise, restated where a renderer would have to break it. C-NO-NETWORK-ADDRESS-COLUMN: no network-address column anywhere, IP addresses are not stored. The only value this may take is false, and the schema is what makes `true` unwritable rather than merely discouraged — the constraint is locked, and a declaration that could say otherwise is a declaration that will.

collects.description: One row per category of personal data the surface actually collects — meaning retained or transmitted, not merely touched in memory. Derived from the surface's own sworn declarations, each row naming which one and when it was read. A `declared` APP declaration must carry at least one row and a `pending` one carries none (see `allOf` below); an extension that transmits nothing carries an empty list and discloses what it HANDLES under `storeDisclosures` instead, because a retention class is not a thing that exists for data that is never stored.

category.description: The Play data-safety category this row belongs to. Kept in that vocabulary because the Play console is the surface with the narrowest, most consequential wording.

purposes.description: Why it is collected, one purpose per entry. C-CONSENT-PER-PURPOSE: consent is recorded PER PURPOSE, append-only, so a purpose list is the unit a grant is checked against and never a single blanket answer.

retentionClass.description: Days, from the locked set. C-RETENTION-PERIODS / [ADR 045]: 400 (raw event-level), 730 (money rail), 1100 (the derived rollup). An enum rather than a number, so a convenience change cannot quietly extend how long personal data is kept.

required.description: Whether the app is unusable without it — the Play console's own question, answered here so the two cannot disagree.

shared.description: Whether it is shared with anybody outside the processors declared below.

basis.description: Why this row says what it says, in a sentence somebody has to be willing to read aloud. The sworn files' discipline: an answer with no basis is a guess with a citation.

source.description: Where the basis was read: a repository path, or an https URL for an external authority.

storeDisclosures.description: EXTENSION SURFACE ONLY, and required there. One row per data category the Chrome Web Store's Privacy practices tab asks about, with the answer that tab is to be given. The tempting answer is the wrong one: under Google's User Data FAQ Q2–Q3, reading a page's title, DOM text or a screenshot IS 'handling user data' even when it never leaves the device, so a tool that reads page content and ticks 'This item does not collect user data' has made a false dashboard statement — and a dashboard answer that contradicts the code is a policy strike at account level. `disposition: local-only` is exactly that case and is what this list exists to render honestly.

category.description: The Chrome Web Store's own category wording, from the Privacy practices tab.

disposition.description: local-only = handled on the device and never transmitted (the box IS ticked, with the local-only explanation). not-collected = the tool does not touch the category at all (the box is not ticked). collected = it leaves the device, in which case the category also owes a `collects` row above with a retention class.

basis.description: Why this answer, in a sentence somebody has to be willing to read aloud to a store reviewer.

limitedUse.description: EXTENSION SURFACE ONLY, and required there. The three Limited Use affirmations the Chrome Web Store dashboard requires, declared rather than retyped into a store console from memory. Each is a promise about behaviour, so each may only be true, and the `basis` says why it is true here — an affirmation whose reason nobody can state is an affirmation nobody should tick.

processors.description: Everyone outside this repository who touches the data. Each `id` must be a row in tooling/legal/provider-register.json — the register is the ONE declaration of who they are, and a second spelling here would be the first to drift. An APP declaration must carry at least one row; an extension that transmits nothing has nobody to name and carries an empty list.

allOf.description: 🔴 THE ARITY FLOORS, PER SURFACE. `collects` and `processors` carried `minItems: 1` unconditionally until the extension surface was added, and NOTHING HERE LOWERS THAT FLOOR FOR A DECLARED APP — it moves into the branch that applies to declared apps, which is where it can be true. A declared app that declares nothing collected and nobody processing is a declaration that graded itself; an extension that transmits nothing has, truthfully, neither. A `pending` app (O-BRICK-STAMPS-NO-PRIVACY-DECLARATION) is the one app that carries no `collects` row, and it says so in its own `state` rather than by an empty list: its notice page publishes no itemised claim at all. tooling/ci/test/app-yaml.test.mjs mutates apps/subscriptiontracker/privacy.yaml to `collects: []` and to `processors: []` and asserts EXIT 1 on both, which is the floor being demonstrated rather than asserted.

anyOf.description: A declared app: a dated declaration, at least one collected category, at least one processor, and no extension-only block.

A pending app, as the brick stamps it: NO collected category, because nobody has read this app's code yet and a guessed row is a claim nobody made. The processors are the providers every app's configuration requires (assert-app-yaml limb 9 holds them), and there is no extension-only block.

An extension: the Chrome Web Store answers are declared and the Limited Use affirmations are present. `collects` may be empty, and is for any tool that transmits nothing. `asOf` is a date here, as it always was.
